canonical_situation: A listed pickup is canceled or has no packages
normalized_description: The driver must distinguish a canceled pickup with no attempt from an attempted pickup at a closed location with no packages.
authoritative_rule: Use pickup reason 24 only for P/U Cancelled - No Attempt Made. Use pickup reason 11 only for Closed - Attempted, No Packages. For an attempted listed pickup with zero packages, FORGE uses Close (Zero Pkg), confirms zero packages, asks for the truthful reason code, and closes with DONE. The sources do not establish reason 11 for every on-site cancellation.
applicability: A listed pickup was canceled before any attempt
A listed pickup was attempted at a closed location and no packages were obtained
The listed pickup must be closed with zero packages
conditions: Reason 24 requires no attempt
Reason 11 requires an attempted pickup at a closed location with no packages
The selected pickup and reason must match what actually happened
exceptions: If the driver arrived but the location was not closed, the reviewed sources do not establish that reason 11 applies merely because someone canceled
Call tags and unlisted pickups are outside this record

required_procedure.action: Determine whether no attempt was made or the pickup was attempted at a closed location with no packages.
Open the correct listed pickup and choose Close (Zero Pkg).
Confirm the Stop Close Summary shows 0 packages and continue.
Select reason 24 for a canceled pickup with no attempt, or reason 11 for a closed location that was attempted with no packages.
Select DONE to close the stop.

prohibited_actions: Do not use reason 24 after an attempt
Do not use reason 11 solely because an on-site contact says canceled when the location is not closed
Do not guess a reason code to close the stop
escalation_requirements: Ask station or service-provider management when an attempted cancellation does not match the source-defined closed/no-packages condition
clarification_requirements: Was any attempt made at the pickup location?

canonical_situation: Delivery package has Appointment, Date Certain, Evening, or Time Definite service
normalized_description: A premium-service package has a date/time commitment and may also have a separate signature requirement that changes release options.
authoritative_rule: Appointment Delivery is guaranteed for the source-stated appointment window on the specified date, requires a signature at delivery, and cannot be driver released or indirectly delivered. Date Certain must be delivered on the specified date and may be driver released only when no Delivery Signature Option applies. Evening Delivery is guaranteed from 5–8 p.m. and may be driver released within that window only when no Delivery Signature Option applies. Time Definite Express services use service-specific commit times that can vary by service, destination type, location, weekday, and Saturday availability. MGB-119 requires delivery by the due time or as soon as safely possible thereafter when timely delivery cannot be made, and a second same-day delivery attempt for packages explicitly identified by the source labels FO, PA, PA+, or M&I.
applicability: Appointment
Date Certain
Evening Delivery

source_authoritative_rule: OP-117 defines on-duty time broadly from readiness to work until relieved of all work responsibility, including station/shipper waiting, inspection/service, driving, loading/unloading/readiness, disabled-vehicle attendance, specified testing, other motor-carrier work, and compensated outside work. canonical_situation: Securing the vehicle and packages during ordinary on-route stops
normalized_description: The driver must secure the vehicle and packages between stops, park and handle packages with situational awareness, and put personal safety first if confronted.
authoritative_rule: OP-117 requires reasonable measures to secure packages at all times and gives on-route parking, awareness, visibility, and confrontation precautions. MGB-119 and the current Security page require doors, including the bulkhead door when applicable, to be locked and windows closed between stops; when the vehicle is not in operation, keys must be removed or secured in a key lockbox.
applicability: Vehicle contains FedEx packages
Driver is parking, leaving, or working from the vehicle between route stops
Packages are being selected or carried from the vehicle
conditions: If confronted or threatened, personal safety takes priority over material items
Vehicle setup and package load must allow quick selection without blocking vision
The key-lockbox alternative applies when the vehicle is not in operation

required_procedure.action: Use a vehicle in good working condition with functioning locks and follow the appropriate pre-trip inspection process.
Park in a highly visible, well-lit location as close to the delivery point as possible and leave enough room to pull or back out in an emergency.
Between stops, lock the doors including the bulkhead door when applicable and close the windows. When the vehicle is not in operation, remove the keys or secure them in a key lockbox.
Keep personal items out of view, remain aware when a vehicle or rear door is open, organize for quick package selection, and do not carry a load that blocks vision.
If you feel threatened while parking, trust your instincts and drive away. If confronted, do not be a hero; cooperate, stay calm, and observe what you safely can because personal safety comes first.

After a confrontation, contact police or 9-1-1 for a life-threatening emergency and contact a FedEx representative. Report violence, threats, or suspicious actions indicating possible violence through station staff, Security, or the FedEx Alert Line.

prohibited_actions: Do not leave packages unsecured
Do not leave doors, the applicable bulkhead door, or windows unsecured between stops
Do not leave keys unsecured when the vehicle is not in operation; remove them or use a key lockbox
Do not jeopardize personal safety to protect material items
Do not overload packages so vision is blocked
escalation_requirements: For a life-threatening emergency after a confrontation, contact police or 9-1-1 and contact a FedEx representative
Report violence, threats, or suspicious actions indicating possible violence to station staff, Security, or through the FedEx Alert Line
Use the separate stolen-vehicle procedure if a branded or shipment-laden vehicle is stolen

canonical_situation: Shipping label address appears incorrect and FORGE offers Edit Address
normalized_description: The driver must distinguish a ZIP Code entered incorrectly after scanning, an incorrect shipping-label address for which the correct recipient address has already been established, and a recipient who is not at the label address.
authoritative_rule: Use the branch that matches the problem. For a ZIP entered incorrectly after scanning, use Edit Address and ReEnter. When the label address is wrong but the correct recipient address has already been established, FORGE provides Stop Details, Stop Options, Edit Address, enter the correct address, ACCEPT, and verify the update. If the recipient is not at the label address, including a moved recipient, use Code 002 and return the package to the station.
applicability: Wrong ZIP Code entered after a package scan
Shipping label carries an incorrect address and the correct recipient address has been established
Recipient is not at the address on the label
conditions: The entered-ZIP branch applies only to a ZIP Code entered incorrectly after scanning
The FORGE label-address example begins with the recipient already located at the correct address
The code-002 branch applies when the recipient is not at the label address, including a moved recipient
exceptions: The reviewed FORGE pages do not define how the correct recipient address is established

required_procedure.action: Determine whether this is an entered-ZIP mistake, an incorrect label with the correct recipient address already established, or a recipient not at the label address.
For an entered-ZIP mistake, open Edit Address and choose ReEnter.
For an established correct address, use Stop Details, Stop Options, Edit Address, enter the correct address, tap ACCEPT, and verify the updated Stop Details.
If the recipient is not at the label address, use Code 002 and return the package to the station.

required_documentation: For an undelivered package, the required package notation matching the scan
prohibited_actions: Do not invent or guess a different recipient address
Do not treat an entered-ZIP correction and a moved recipient as the same branch
escalation_requirements: If the correct recipient address has not already been established, stop and obtain current station or management direction before changing the delivery point.

normalized_description: A package is not on the current manifest; the driver must branch based on whether station or management assigned it and the label establishes the address.
authoritative_rule: If station or management assigned the package and its label establishes the address, scan it as Delivery and use the label-supported stop details. If not, deliver it when close to the address, add it to the map for a later route stop, or ask the BC for advice if the address has already been passed.

required_procedure.action: Determine whether station or management assigned the package and whether the label establishes the delivery address.
If yes, scan the package, select Delivery, enter the label-supported stop details, and choose the actual business or residential type.
If no and the address is close to where you are already delivering, deliver it.
If no and the address will be on your route later, add it to your map and deliver it when you get there.
If no and you already passed the address, check with your BC for advice.

prohibited_actions: Do not invent an address

normalized_description: FORGE displays Authorization Failed during login because device-time validation found the device clock outside the allowed comparison range.
authoritative_rule: During login, FORGE compares the device clock with server time. When server time is available, a difference of more than 24 hours ahead or behind blocks authorization. exceptions: When current server time is unavailable, the source says a device more than 24 hours ahead of stored time may proceed.

canonical_situation: Performing the unified vehicle pre-trip or post-trip safety inspection
normalized_description: A driver needs the owner-approved unified checklist for pre-trip, post-trip, what-to-check, or DOT-standard vehicle inspection questions.
authoritative_rule: Complete the unified vehicle inspection. For tire tread, front/steering tires on a truck require at least 4/32 inch and all other tires require at least 2/32 inch in a major tread groove. Use a tread-depth gauge for the actual threshold. The penny test is only a rough 2/32-inch screen and cannot prove a steering tire meets 4/32 inch. If any tire or other inspected item is unsafe or not working correctly, notify the BC immediately and pull over or park safely.
applicability: Pre-trip inspection
Post-trip inspection
General vehicle-safety or DOT-standard inspection question

required_procedure.action: Check brakes; all lights and signals; mirrors; windshield and wipers; horn; and steering.
Check every tire for tread, pressure, cuts, exposed material, separation, leaks, and other damage.
Use a tread-depth gauge in a major tread groove: front/steering tires require at least 4/32 inch and other tires require at least 2/32 inch. Do not measure on tie bars, humps, or fillets.

For a rough 2/32-inch screen only, place a penny into the groove with Lincoln’s head upside down. If the top of his head is visible, the tire is at or below the replacement threshold. Do not use this test to approve a steering tire; verify 4/32 inch with a gauge.
Check fluid levels, fuel, seatbelt, emergency equipment including the fire extinguisher and warning triangles, cargo securement, and general body condition or leaks.
If anything is unsafe or not working correctly, notify your BC immediately and pull over or park in a safe area.

prohibited_actions: Do not continue without notifying the BC when an inspected item is not working correctly
Do not approve a front/steering tire with less than 4/32 inch in a major tread groove.
Do not approve another tire with less than 2/32 inch in a major tread groove.
Do not use the penny test as proof that a front/steering tire meets the 4/32-inch requirement.
escalation_requirements: Notify the BC immediately for any item that is not working correctly

exceptions: This is not the no-barcode or Key Enter procedure

Search for no more than 5–8 minutes.
If you find the package later on the route, attempt delivery then.
If the address is too far out of the way when you find it, call your BC for advice.

canonical_situation: Explaining the conceptual difference between DSR and ISR
normalized_description: A new driver wants a plain-language comparison rather than the operational signature-service selector.
authoritative_rule: DSR requires an in-person signature from someone at the labeled delivery address, so a neighbor at another address cannot sign. ISR can allow an eligible neighbor’s signature when the required indirect-delivery scan, address, signature, and door-tag documentation are completed.
applicability: The driver asks what DSR means
The driver asks how DSR differs from ISR or an ordinary signature
exceptions: ASR, alcohol, controlled-substance, appointment, and other stricter services have separate requirements

required_procedure.action: For DSR, obtain an in-person signature from someone at the labeled address; do not use a neighbor at another address.
For ISR, an eligible neighbor can be used only through the documented indirect-delivery path, including the indirect address, signature, and scanned door tag left at the labeled address.

prohibited_actions: Do not treat DSR and ISR as interchangeable.
Do not tell a driver that any neighbor can sign for ISR without the required indirect-delivery documentation.

canonical_situation: A driver asks what a diamond-shaped hazmat label on a package means
normalized_description: The driver recognizes a hazardous-material diamond but needs its meaning and the immediate paperwork/procedure boundary.
authoritative_rule: Drivers may call it a hazmat placard, but on an individual package it is generally a hazardous-material label or marking. The diamond communicates the hazard class or type, such as flammable, corrosive, or toxic, and some markings include an identification number. Treat the package as hazmat: verify the applicable manifest and package paperwork, including SF-136 when required, and follow the relevant hazmat procedure rather than ordinary-package handling.
applicability: A diamond-shaped hazardous-material label or marking appears on an individual package
The driver calls the package symbol a hazmat placard
conditions: The exact paperwork and procedure depend on the package and hazard class
exceptions: This definition alone does not establish acceptance, loading, delivery, leakage, incompatibility, placarding-weight, or emergency procedure

required_procedure.action: Recognize the diamond as a hazardous-material package label or marking and identify the displayed hazard class or type.
Verify that the applicable manifest and package paperwork match, including SF-136 when required.
Use the relevant hazmat procedure for the package; do not treat it as an ordinary package.

required_documentation: Applicable package paperwork, including SF-136 when required
prohibited_actions: Do not ignore the diamond label or marking.
Do not infer a complete hazmat procedure from the symbol alone.
Do not treat package labels and vehicle placards as technically identical.
escalation_requirements: Use a FedEx Safety/Hazmat specialist or station compliance owner when the label, paperwork, or applicable procedure is uncertain

canonical_overrides.more_info_answer: These are three different moments: cancel before finalization, Delete Scan after the scan commits but before delivery, and misdelivery recovery after a completed wrong delivery.

The other packages look fine
